units.source_text: 我没能看见鹤川的遗体，也没能参加他的葬礼，我困惑于不知怎样才能在自己的心中确认锥川已经死亡了。

en.t: I was unable to see Tsurukawa's body, and I was unable to attend his funeral; I was bewildered, not knowing how I could confirm in my own heart that Tsurukawa had died.

units.source_text: 昔日他裹着白衬衫在透过树叶缝隙筛落下来的阳光下荡起波浪的腹部，如今依然在燃烧。

en.t: His abdomen, once wrapped in a white shirt and rippling beneath the sunlight sifted down through gaps in the leaves, was still burning even now.

units.source_text: 谁能想像到像他那样专为光明而制造的、最适合于接受光明的肉体和精神，会被埋葬在墓土里安息呢？

en.t: Who could imagine that a body and spirit like his, made especially for light and most suited to receiving light, would be buried in grave soil and lie at rest there?

units.source_text: 他身上毫无夭折的征兆，尽管他能逃脱地所生的不安和忧愁，但他却毫不具备类似死的因素。

en.t: There was not the slightest sign in him of an early death; though he could escape the anxieties and sorrows born of the earth, he possessed nothing at all resembling an element of death.

units.source_text: 也许正是因为这个缘故他才摔然故去的吧。

en.t: Perhaps it was precisely for that reason that he passed away so suddenly.

units.source_text: 也许就像纯血种的动物生命是很脆弱一样，鹤川光是由生的纯粹成分制造出来的，因此无法防御死。

en.t: Perhaps, just as the lives of purebred animals are very fragile, Tsurukawa was made only from the pure elements of life, and therefore could not defend himself against death.

units.source_text: 相反，应受诅咒的长寿却仿佛得到了保证似的。

en.t: By contrast, an accursed longevity seemed almost to have been guaranteed.
